Job Description:
Role Purpose:
The Logistics Officer is responsible for the efficient, timely, and cost-effective coordination of logistics operations, with specific responsibility for interplant transfers, movement of bulk materials from designated storage areas to plants, and rail transfers. The role ensures the smooth flow of materials and products by effectively planning, coordinating, monitoring, documenting, and communicating assigned movements, while proactively addressing delays and minimizing storage costs, transport inefficiencies, and supply disruptions.
Key Duties and Responsibilities:
Interplant Transfer Coordination
Coordinate the movement of raw materials, finished goods, and other products between company plants, depots, and other designated storage areas.
Liaise with the sending and receiving plants to confirm movement requirements, quantities, loading schedules, and delivery priorities.
Coordinate vehicle allocation and dispatch in line with approved transport plans.
Track vehicles from loading point to destination and provide regular status updates.
Follow up on delivery documentation, including delivery notes, transfer documents, weighbridge tickets, and proof of delivery.
Identify and escalate delays, vehicle breakdowns, loading challenges, or other operational issues affecting transfers.
Maintain accurate records of all interplant movements.
Warehouse/ storage areas to Plant Logistics
Coordinate the movement of bulk cargo from the designated loading areas to the respective plant or designated warehouse.
Liaise with the logistics officer- Imports and transporters to ensure cargo is moved within the required timelines.
Monitor cargo availability, customs clearance status, transport allocation, and delivery schedules.
Ensure relevant delivery and transport documentation is properly captured and filed.
Escalate potential delays that may affect production, customer supply, or logistics costs.
Rail Coordination
Support the planning and coordination of rail movements from the rail terminal to the plants
Liaise with railway operators and internal stakeholders on rail movement schedules.
Monitor wagon loading, dispatch, arrival, and offloading activities.
Track rail consignments and provide regular movement status updates.
Coordinate with the receiving plant to ensure readiness for arrival and offloading.
Follow up on rail delays, wagon availability, documentation issues, and operational constraints.
Maintain accurate records of rail movements and associated documentation.
Transporter Coordination
Communicate daily transport requirements to appointed transporters.
Follow up on vehicle availability, driver details, vehicle positioning, loading, and delivery.
Monitor transporter performance against agreed service requirements.
Report recurring service failures, delays, or non-compliance to the Logistics Manager
Support the verification of transport documentation and delivery records.
Logistics Tracking & Reporting
Maintain daily logistics movement trackers covering road, rail, interplant, and plant deliveries.
Prepare daily/weekly logistics status reports as required.
Monitor key logistics performance indicators, including:
On-time delivery
Vehicle turnaround time
Port-to-plant transit time
Rail transit time
Loading/offloading delays
Storage exposure
Pending deliveries
Proof of delivery compliance
Maintain an updated record of outstanding and delayed movements.
Support reconciliation of transport and delivery records.
Documentation & Compliance
Ensure logistics documentation is complete, accurate, and properly filed.
Verify delivery notes, transfer documents, weighbridge tickets, container details, and proof of delivery.
Follow company logistics procedures, transport policies, and safety requirements.
Ensure movements comply with applicable statutory and company requirements.
Escalate documentation gaps or compliance issues promptly.
Job Requirements
Academic Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Transport Management, Business Management, or a related field.
Professional Qualifications
Certification in Fleet/ Logistics or Transport Management is an added advantage.
Experience
Minimum 3–5 years’ experience in logistics, warehouse, and transport operations management.
Experience in transport coordination, fleet tracking, warehouse operations, or distribution will be an added advantage.
Exposure to road, rail, containerized cargo, or interplant logistics is desirable.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other standard office applications.
Knowledge of ERP/logistics management systems is an added advantage.
Key Attributes and competencies
Strong coordination, communication, and follow-up skills.
Good organizational, time-management, and attention-to-detail skills.
Ability to manage multiple logistics movements in a fast-paced environment.
Strong problem-solving, escalation, and stakeholder management skills.
Basic analytical and reporting capabilities
Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
High level of integrity, accountability, and ownership.

Research and analysis

Design and support primary research using appropriate qualitative and quantitative methods, including
interviews, focus groups, surveys, consultations and case studies. Support research commissioning and quality assurance.

Identify where evidence is incomplete or contested and advise on the implications for AfricaNenda Foundation’s position.
Maintain a clear record of approvals, versions, sources, research ethics requirements and intellectualproperty arrangements.
Advocacy strategy and execution

Support the Director in developing, executing and periodically refining AfricaNenda Foundation’s advocacy strategy, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and approved institutional positions.

Job Title: Senior Monitoring, Reporting, Evaluation, Learning and Adaptation (MRELA) Officer
Job Description:
Program / Department Summary
Mercy Corps is seeking a Senior Monitoring, Reporting, Evaluation, Learning and Adaptation (MRELA) Officer for the FCDO-funded Border Security Programme (BSP), in Kenya. Irregular migration and associated criminal activity in East Africa remain a complex and escalating challenge which leads to significant exploitation of vulnerable people on the move. The planned Border Security Programme will take a multifaceted approach – integrating ‘prevention’, ‘prepare/protect’ and ‘pursue’. An important purpose of this programme is to support the pursuit of human traffickers and smugglers who are exploiting vulnerable populations on the move. Initial interventions will take place in the Kenya border regions, with planned and phased expansion to Uganda, Ethiopia and possibly Somalia border areas.
General Position Summary
The Senior MRELA Officer plays a key role in Mercy Corps' programme quality assurance, accountability, documentation, and learning function, providing direct support to the BSP programme. Reporting to the Programme MRELA Manager, the position holder supports the design and implementation of monitoring, reporting, evaluation, learning, and adaptation activities, including ensuring data quality, generating evidence for adaptive management, and supporting accountability to participants, partners, and the donor.
The role combines hands-on data collection, facilitation of learning processes, and capacity strengthening of programme staff and implementing partners. Given the sensitivity of the programme's context and the vulnerability of its target population, the Senior MRELA Officer is expected to demonstrate a strong commitment to ethical and responsible data practices throughout all aspects of their work.
Essential Job Responsibilities
STRATEGY SUPPORT AND MRELA SYSTEM IMPLEMENTATION
Lead the development, testing, refinement and roll-out of MRELA tools and system components for the BSP programme, including data collection instruments, indicator tracking tools, and data management systems.
Contribute to the development and review of intervention designs, sector strategies, and the MRELA framework.
Provide technical inputs into programme logic, theories of change, and review documents, helping to refine approaches to reflect monitoring evidence and learning.
Support the program teams and partners in ensuring adherence to Mercy Corps' MEL Minimum standards.
Support the MRELA manager in translating MRELA strategy and framework into practical systems, tools, processes, and workplans across the BSP programme.
MONITORING & DATA MANAGEMENT
Develop and maintain an accurate and up-to-date documentation of progress against agreed progress markers, including evidence of emerging changes.
Validate and verify results data received from implementing partners and grantees against primary source documents while applying systematic data quality checks.
Implement a Data Quality Assessment (DQA) plan; conduct periodic DQAs and document findings, tracking corrective actions through to resolution.
Conduct monitoring visits to programme sites and partner locations, collecting supplementary data and qualitative information, both independently and as part of programme teams.
Maintain a secure, well-organized data management system that enables timely retrieval, analysis, and aggregation of programme data, in compliance with Mercy Corps' data protection and responsible data policies.
Ensure monitoring approaches are protection-sensitive and responsive to the confidentiality and safety needs of beneficiaries in a trafficking and irregular migration context.
Work with the MRELA Manager and programme staff to ensure activities are on track against targets, surfacing data-driven concerns through regular planning and review meetings.
Lead the design and implementation of quantitative and qualitative data collection, including development and testing of data collection instruments,configuration and management of digital data collection tools in CommCare, training and supervision of data collectors, data quality assurance, data cleaning, analysis and interpretation of findings.
EVALUATIONS AND ASSESSMENTS
Support the planning, design, coordination, and supervision of programme assessments, evaluations and thematic research.
Take lead in developing core evaluation assets including Scopes of Work (SoWs), survey instruments, sampling methodologies, data collection protocols, and analysis frameworks for evaluations and assessments.
Support in the recruitment and training of data collection teams and enumerators.
Provide technical and operational oversight todata collectorion processes, ensuring adherence to ethical and data protection standards.
Support or manage the recruitment and day-to-day supervision of external evaluation consultants where required, ensuring deliverables meet quality standards and timelines.
Contribute to and review evaluation reports, ensuring findings are evidence-based, clearly presented, and accompanied by actionable recommendations.
REPORTING
Coordinate results reporting with consortium partners, tracking deadlines and ensuring adherence to reporting formats, indicator definitions, and quality standards.
Consolidate, analyse, and synthesize quantitative and qualitative results data for donor and internal reporting.
Contribute clear evidence-based narrative against agreed performance indicators.
Review partner reports for data accuracy, completeness, internal consistency, and alignment with the programme's monitoring framework before consolidation and submission.
Maintain well-organized documentation of all monitoring data, evaluation reports, and supporting evidence, ensuring all reported results are traceable to source documentation.
LEARNING, ADAPTATION, AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT
Maintain an up-to-date database that accurately reflects progress against programme indicators and learning outcomes, ensuring data is accessible to the programme team.
Facilitate or co-facilitate regular programme reflection and learning events to enable the team to analyse monitoring data and translate findings into adaptive management decisions.
Document and support dissemination of programme lessons, good practices, and emerging insights in accessible formats for internal and external audiences.
Contribute to the programme's learning and research agenda, supporting the identification of priority learning questions and the design of activities to address them.
CAPACITY BUILDING
Assess MRELA capacity gaps among grantees and provide targeted training and coaching to build their ability to implement programme monitoring tools, manage data accurately, and produce quality reports.
Support grantees in developing and maintaining effective MEL systems that meet programme standard.
Build the capacity of all relevant team members to implement program-monitoring tools, accurately enter program data into relevant databases, and use monitoring evidence in programme planning and decision-making.
Advise on and support the testing and adoption of appropriate digital technologies to improve the efficiency, accuracy, and security of MRELA functions.
STAKEHOLDER COORDINATION
Maintain an active advisory relationship with the programme team, guiding staff toward robust, relevant, and ethical data collection practices at all stages of programme implementation.
Establish and maintain strong working relationships with partner MRELA focal points to support coordinated MRELA activities.
Participate in ongoing MRELA advisory and support activities for BSP programme staff and local partners, providing feedback on data quality and results at key programme milestones.
Represent the MRELA function in programme planning and review meetings, presenting data-driven insights to support evidence-informed decision-making.
OTHER
Conduct himself/herself both professionally and personally in such a manner as to bring credit to Mercy Corps and to not jeopardize its humanitarian mission or programming activities.
Perform other relevant duties as assigned.
SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES
Actively learns safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.
Supervisory Responsibility
Enumerators from time to time.
Accountability
Reports Directly To:
Programme MRELA Manager.
Works Directly With:
MRELA staff, Programme leads; Programme partners
Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders
Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.
Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills
Bachelor's degree in social science, statistics, business administration, or a relevant field.
Minimum 5 years of professional experience in programme monitoring and evaluation in an international development, humanitarian, or related context.
Solid understanding of MEL concepts and frameworks, including programme logic, results chains, logframes, theories of change, and participatory monitoring approaches.
Demonstrated ability to implement quantitative and qualitative data collection tools and working knowledge of sampling techniques.
Strong data analysis skills; ability to work with both quantitative and qualitative datasets.

Experience with digital data collection platforms (preferably CommCare and Power BI)
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; ability to present complex data clearly and accessibly for diverse audiences.

Job Description:
The Learning Experience Designer (LXD) plays a critical role in improving partner and customer capability, confidence and product adoption through exceptional learning experiences.
Working as part of the Training & Support team, you will lead and drive the end to end learning experience from learner research and discovery through to design evaluation and continuous improvement ensuring learning evolves alongside our software and our user needs. You'll translate subject matter expert (SME) authored content into engaging, learner-centred experiences that make technical concepts simple, accessible and easy to apply.
Working closely with the Head of Partner and Customer Enablement, Partner and Customer Enablement Leads, Product teams, Clinical Leads, Partnership teams and our Learning Platform Specialist, you'll design scalable learning solutions that support onboarding, product adoption and ongoing capability development. Success in this role means creating learning experiences that measurably improve learner confidence, customer adoption and organisation outcomes, while establishing high standards for learning quality, governance and continuous improvement across our learning ecosystem.

Experience in Learning Experience Design or Curriculum Design, with an education background, teaching qualification and experience as a trainer or facilitator.

Strong curriculum design, lesson planning, storyboarding and learning documentation skills with excellent learning content writing that simplifies complex technical concepts, strong visual communication and attention to detail.
Strong grounding in adult learning theory and learning experience design methodologies (e.g. ADDIE, Kolb Experiential Learning), with experience designing assessments, knowledge checks and certification programmes, and applying learner research, analytics and evaluation frameworks to measurable outcomes.
Experience collaborating with Product Design or UX teams in a software organisation — comfortable reading designs and prototypes (e.g. Figma, Claude Design) and working within an established design system.
Excellent written communication, facilitation, stakeholder management and relationship-building skills with proven collaboration in multidisciplinary teams, a learner-first mindset and a proactive, self-motivated commitment to continuous improvement.

Experience using AI-assisted learning design and content development tools
Experience creating multimedia learning using authoring tools
Experience supporting organisational change management initiatives.
Experience working within Agile delivery environments.
BA or MA in Education, Applied Linguistics or a related discipline.
Experience with SafetyCulture LMS or similar learning platforms

The Pensions Administration Assistant is responsible for providing administrative and logistical support for the effective management and administration of the Pension Scheme, ensuring operational efficiency, adherence to established governance frameworks and alignment with the Pensions Administration Department’s policies, guidelines and strategic objectives.
The role serves as an entry-level professional position within the Pensions function and supports the development of future Pensions Administration professionals.
KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Pension Administration Support
Maintain accurate and up-to-date Scheme records and files, including records of the section’s activities.
Support the Assistant Pensions Administration Officer in calculating member benefits and processing pension-related transactions.
Ensure that all standard pension administration procedures are adhered to and that routine administrative tasks are completed accurately and within the required timelines.
Provide regular updates to the Pensions team on work in progress and outstanding activities.
Assist the Pensions team in maintaining effective pension administration processes, controls and compliance.
Member and Stakeholder Support
Support the Pensions team in liaising with Scheme members and their dependants.
Assist the Assistant Pensions Administration Officer in responding to member queries received by telephone, email and face-to-face.
Respond to clients in a timely and professional manner, providing relevant and accurate information.
Support effective stakeholder engagement and contribute to the delivery of quality member services.
Scheme Communication and Member Engagement
Support the Assistant Pensions Administration Officer in developing and coordinating Scheme communications to members.
Provide administrative and logistical support in organizing the Annual General Meeting for Scheme members.
Assist in ensuring that members receive timely and accurate information on Scheme matters and activities.
Records, Compliance and Controls
Maintain complete, accurate and properly organized Scheme records and files.
Ensure compliance with established procedures, policies and administrative controls.
Maintain appropriate records of member queries, actions and follow-ups to support effective service delivery, accountability and audit requirements.
Identify and escalate issues that may affect service delivery, compliance or operational controls.
Team and Departmental Support
Work effectively as part of the Pensions Administration team to support the Department’s activities and objectives.
Provide general administrative support to the Pensions Administration function as required.
Assist in coordinating team activities and following up on agreed actions to ensure timely completion.
Meetings, Reporting and Coordination
Record accurate minutes of team meetings, including key discussions, decisions and agreed action points.
Follow up on outstanding actions arising from team meetings to support continuous improvement in service delivery.
Provide regular reports and updates to the Assistant Pensions Administration Officer on activities, issues and work in progress.
Support the Department with administrative, logistical, budget and audit-related activities as required.
Budget and Audit Support
Provide administrative support in the preparation and maintenance of documentation required for budget monitoring and audit purposes.
Maintain appropriate supporting records and documentation to facilitate internal and external audit requirements.
Assist with the coordination and provision of information required for pension administration reviews, compliance activities and audits.
Other Responsibilities
Perform any other duties as may be assigned by the Assistant Pensions Administration Officer, Pensions Administration Officer and the Senior Pensions Administration Officer.
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
Pensions Administration Processing
Accuracy and completeness of pension administration transactions and records.
Timeliness of processing member requests, benefits and pension administration activities.
Completeness and accuracy of supporting documentation for pension administration transactions.
Records and Reconciliations
Timeliness and accuracy of Scheme records and administrative reconciliations.
Number of outstanding or unresolved discrepancies in Scheme records.
Accuracy and completeness of member files and supporting documentation.
Reporting
Timeliness of work-in-progress updates and administrative reports.
Accuracy and completeness of information provided to the Assistant Pensions Administration Officer.
Timely escalation of outstanding issues, discrepancies and member-related matters.
Compliance and Controls
Compliance with Scheme rules, pension administration policies, procedures and established controls.
Accuracy and completeness of records maintained for audit and compliance purposes.
Number of audit findings or compliance issues attributable to the role.
Member and Stakeholder Service Delivery
Responsiveness to member and stakeholder queries and requests.
Timeliness and accuracy of information provided to Scheme members and their dependants.
Quality and professionalism of support provided to members and internal stakeholders.
Administrative and Team Support
Timely completion of routine administrative and pension administration tasks.
Effectiveness of support provided in meetings, Scheme member events and communications.
Accuracy and timeliness of meeting minutes and follow-up on agreed action points.
JOB SPECIFICATIONS
Academic Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Insurance, Business Administration, Actuarial Science or any relevant or equivalent qualifications from a recognised university.
Professional Qualifications
Actively pursuing Professional Qualificationssuch as ACII, AIIK or equivalent or any other recognized
Pensions Administration professional qualification.
Experience
A minimum of one (1) year relevant experience in Pension Administration.
Knowledge and Competencies
Technical Competencies
Pension administration and member records
Pension contributions and reconciliations
ERP/pensions systems
Budget monitoring
Internal controls
Microsoft Excel
Behavioral Competencies
Attention to detail.
Analytical skills.
Accountability.
Planning and organization.
Communication skills.
Teamwork.
Professionalism.
Integrity.

Job Description:
About the Job
The Network Development Associate based in Africa will play a key role in strengthening engagement, communication, and coordination across the HelpAge Global Network. This is an exciting opportunity to support a growing and strategically important area of work that helps connect members, amplify their voices, and enable collaboration across regions.
The postholder will work closely with the Network Platform Manager, Africa Regional Adviser and Thematic Advisers to support member engagement, knowledge sharing, and the effective functioning of the HelpAge Digital Portal. The role will help build stronger relationships across the network, improve information flows, and contribute to more connected, visible and collaborative ways of working, particularly across Africa and within the wider global network.
Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities
Network Engagement and support to the Network Platform (50%)
Working with the Network Platform Team, strengthen communication and coordination between HelpAge and network members, particularly across Africa, alongside the Regional Advisers and Thematic Advisers.
Support and facilitate knowledge sharing, collaboration and peer learning across the network.
Support the curation, management and updating of the HelpAge digital portal, providing administrative backend support and firstline user support.
Help organise thematic sessions, webinars, peer learning events, and cross‑network exchanges.
Support in the development of newsletters and additional communications content for network members and other stakeholders.
Support member applications, onboarding, and induction processes.
Maintain accurate member information and mailing lists on HelpAge CONNECT (Hosted by salesforce) and SharePoint.
Support the coordination of Network Development Team meetings and provide other administrative support to the Network Development Team as needed.
Support in tracking engagement and participation trends across the membership.
Regional Network Engagement, Communications and Administrative Support for the Regional Adviser, Africa (50%)
Support communication and engagement with potential and existing network members across Africa, helping maintain strong information flows between members, the Regional Adviser and cross organisational teams and the wider network.
Provide logistical and administrative support for regional meetings, webinars, learning events and member engagements.
Prepare and disseminate agendas, invitations, briefing materials and meeting notes, and maintain agreed records and documentation.
Support communications, member liaison and event administration for regional initiatives, including the Africa Ageing Conference, Africa Coordination Mechanism and resource mobilisation where required.
Collect and maintain member engagement data, feedback and participation information to support reporting, learning and continuous improvement.
Coordinate translation and interpretation arrangements for regional communications and events where needed.
Gather stories, case studies and learning content from network members and partners across Africa.
Develop communications and visibility materials that strengthen member engagement and showcase network impact across the region, including ensuring up-to-date information in digital and website platforms.
Maintain regional communications channels including social media pages and support knowledge sharing within Africa and across the wider HelpAge network.
Contribute to the strategic planning and reporting processes for Africa region including leading on communication and knowledge management plan for Africa.
Skills and experience required
At least 3–5 years of experience supporting regional and global network coordination processes, member engagement, event coordination, and administrative functions, ideally within international development, civil society, humanitarian settings, or multi-stakeholder environments.
Experience in supporting logistical planning and coordination of sub-regional, regional and global meetings, workshops, webinars, learning events and strategic convenings.
Good IT skills and familiarity with digital collaboration, communication and data visualization tools.
Strong written communication skills with the ability to produce clear, concise documents, including meeting minutes and action points.
Experience supporting online events, webinars, virtual meetings and knowledge‑sharing processes.
Basic design and editing skills; familiarity with Canva, WordPress and Mailchimp is desirable.
Experience producing and supporting newsletters, digital communications and managing social media channels.
Ability to draft and edit news updates, communication content and articles in English.
Ability to troubleshoot basic digital platforms, connectivity or login issues during online meetings and events.
Fluency in English (written and spoken); additional African UNION or UN language are desirable
Ability to manage competing priorities, work under pressure and meet deadlines.
Strong organizational and time‑management skills.
Good interpersonal skills and experience working in cross‑cultural settings.
High level of discretion when handling sensitive information.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
Cultural sensitivity and respect for diversity.
Company Address: Development Centre, Off Lower Kabete Road, Off Shanzu Road, PO Box 14888 00800, Westlands, Nairobi, Kenya

Job Description:
ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY AND RESPONSIBILITIES
As the Manager, Portfolio Analytics, you will lead a team of Investments Business Analysts and Graduate Trainees to drive data-informed investment decisions, strengthen portfolio performance and risk monitoring, and lead strategic investment systems and analytics initiatives.
In this role, you will provide analytical oversight and decision support for credit risk management, strengthen portfolio and financial data architecture, and own executive-level portfolio reporting. You will serve as a strategic partner to cross-functional and cross-country leaders, translating complex data into actionable insights that improve investment decisions and portfolio outcomes.
You will also lead core digital transformation initiatives to streamline data flows between investment operational and accounting systems, strengthen data quality and governance, and improve operational efficiency, portfolio visibility and portfolio quality across Inkomoko.
Roles and Responsibilities
Team Leadership & Development: Lead, mentor and develop a high-performing team of Business Analysts and Graduate Trainees, setting clear objectives, performance standards and development plans while building a culture of analytical excellence, ownership and continuous improvement.
Portfolio Performance Analytics: Lead analysis of portfolio performance across key indicators including disbursements, collections, PAR, defaults, write-offs, recoveries, and provisioning. Identify performance trends, drivers, risks and opportunities, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
Portfolio Planning, Forecasting & Scenario Analysis: Support portfolio forecasting, target setting and scenario modelling to support portfolio growth.Provide forward-looking assessments of expected portfolio performance under different business and risk scenarios.
Risk Analytics & Early Warning: Develop and maintain portfolio risk monitoring and early-warning indicators to identify emerging deterioration, concentration risks and other changes in portfolio quality. Lead stress testing and scenario analysis and provide timely escalation of material risks.
Credit & Investment Decision Support: Provide timely, high-quality analytical support to Portfolio and Credit Risk Management, using data and insights to inform underwriting, client selection, portfolio growth, collections, risk mitigation and other investment decisions.
Executive Reporting & Insights: Own internal and external executive-level reporting on portfolio investments, ensuring executive leadership, Board members, country leadership and external partners receive accurate, timely and insightful reporting. Translate complex portfolio data into clear conclusions, forward-looking insights and actionable recommendations.
Business Intelligence & Reporting: Design, develop and maintain automated dashboards, analytical tools and reporting solutions that provide accessible, reliable and timely visibility into portfolio performance, risk and strategic KPIs.
Data & Systems Transformation: Support the DT team on data and systems change initiatives that strengthen credit risk infrastructure, data integration, portfolio analytics and reporting automation. Ensure analytical requirements are clearly translated into effective system and data solutions.
Cross-Country Collaboration: Partner with country Investment teams and leadership to strengthen investment systems, data quality, portfolio monitoring and reporting, while ensuring consistent analytical standards and timely resolution of data and reporting issues.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with all regional functions to ensure effective data flows, aligned methodologies and high-quality analytical inputs across the organisation.
Data Governance, Quality & Audit Readiness: Establish and enforce data quality, governance and analytical quality-assurance standards. Ensure portfolio reporting and analysis are accurate, traceable, reproducible and aligned with internal policies, regulatory requirements and audit standards.
Analytical Team Operating Model: Establish the team's analytical priorities, delivery calendar, quality standards and ways of working, ensuring the Portfolio Analytics function consistently delivers high-value insights to support organisational and portfolio objectives.
Requirements
Who we are looking for;
Bachelor’s degree in Business Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field (relevant professional charter preferred).
4+ years of progressive experience in business analytics, financial analysis, portfolio management, or credit risk management.
Experience managing, leading, or mentoring analytics professionals and junior team members.
Demonstrated track record of leading technology integration or systems change management projects in a financial or investment context.
Technical Skills
Data Analysis & Modeling: Expert proficiency in analytics coding language and tools. Python plus SQL will be an added advantage in addition to tools knowledge on MS Excel, financial modeling, credit risk modeling, and portfolio stress testing.
Data Visualization: Advanced mastery of enterprise BI and dashboarding platforms such as Power BI, Holistics, or Tableau.
Systems Architecture & Data Integration: Deep understanding of data pipelines, core banking/investment platform integrations, and financial data flows and workings of APIs.
Project Management: Proficiency in project tracking methodologies, quality assurance, and workflow documentation tools.
Competencies
We are looking for someone who;
Leads Teams - Aligns the team with common objectives derived from the organizational strategy, fosters a shared mindset, and celebrates wins while recognizing team efforts.
Builds Trust - Holds self and others accountable by clearly outlining responsibilities, tracking results, delegating effectively, building independence and demonstrating care for others, and being consistent in actions.
Relationship Management - Establishes and maintains strong relationships with key stakeholders, partners, and community leaders, while anticipating and balancing the needs of multiple stakeholders.
Benefits
What You'll Get
This role is inside a high-growth, mission-driven social enterprise. By joining, you’ll access:
Meaningful work that directly contributes to sustainable livelihoods and job creation across East and Central Africa.
Competitive salary, and potential Performance-based bonus
Incredible company culture, with opportunities for learning and growth
Diverse colleagues across the region, and policies that demonstrate commitment to equity and inclusion
A dynamic and entrepreneurial team environment committed to innovation and social impact
Health insurance for self and family
Staff savings and provident fund, negotiated bank rates for long-term employees
Generous annual leave, parental leave, and sabbatical options.
Job Field: Data, Business Analysis and AI,ICT / Computer

Job Description:
Job Role
The Operations Manager will oversee the day-to-day operations of the automotive business, ensuring efficient coordination of sales, workshop/service operations, inventory, procurement, customer service and administration. The role will focus on improving operational efficiency, controlling costs, maintaining service quality and supporting achievement of the company's business objectives.
PURPOSE OF THE ROLE
To provide effective leadership and coordination of the company's operations by ensuring that people, processes, inventory, customer service and resources are managed efficiently. The role is responsible for driving operational excellence, minimizing inefficiencies, supporting revenue growth and ensuring that customers receive quality and timely automotive products and services.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Operations Management
Oversee the day-to-day operations of the automotive business.
Develop and implement effective operational procedures and controls.
Coordinate activities between sales, workshop/service, stores, procurement and administration.
Monitor operational performance and identify areas requiring improvement.
Ensure company policies and procedures are consistently followed.
Sales & Business Operations
Work closely with the sales team to support achievement of sales and revenue targets.
Monitor sales performance and provide regular updates to management.
Identify operational challenges affecting sales performance and customer conversion.
Support implementation of strategies aimed at improving business performance.
Monitor customer orders, product/vehicle availability and delivery timelines.
Workshop & Service Coordination
Oversee the coordination of workshop and service activities.
Ensure vehicles are properly received, assessed, serviced/repaired and released within agreed timelines.
Monitor service quality and customer satisfaction.
Coordinate with technicians and service personnel to resolve operational challenges.
Ensure proper documentation of inspections, repairs and service activities.
Inventory & Stock Management
Oversee the management of vehicles, spare parts, accessories and other automotive stock.
Monitor stock levels and coordinate timely replenishment.
Ensure proper recording and storage of inventory.
Conduct regular stock checks and reconciliations.
Minimize stock losses, damages, overstocking and stock-outs.
Procurement & Supplier Management
Coordinate procurement of automotive parts, equipment and operational supplies.
Work with approved suppliers to ensure timely delivery and competitive pricing.
Monitor supplier performance and quality.
Maintain proper procurement records and documentation.
Financial & Cost Control
Monitor operational expenses and identify opportunities for cost reduction.
Ensure operations are conducted within approved budgets.
Monitor wastage, losses and unnecessary expenditure.
Work with the finance team to support accurate operational financial reporting.
QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Automotive Management, or a related field.
At least 4–6 years of relevant experience in operations management, preferably within the automotive industry.
Previous experience in automotive sales, dealership, workshop, spare parts or vehicle-related operations is an added advantage.
Proven experience supervising and coordinating teams.
Experience in inventory, procurement, budgeting and operational reporting.
Good understanding of automotive business operations and customer service.

Job Description:
Position Summary
The Compliance Intern will provide administrative and coordination support to the Compliance function, with primary responsibility for maintaining and updating Compliance trackers, calendars, records, and related documentation. The role will support audit and assurance administration, compliance monitoring, statutory and regulatory compliance tracking, and other Compliance activities as assigned.
The intern will be expected to ensure that assigned trackers and calendars are current based on information received and to actively follow up on missing or overdue updates. Where gaps, inconsistencies, or potential compliance concerns are identified, these will be escalated to the Compliance Manager or Compliance Officer for substantive review and action.
Key Responsibilities
Audit and Assurance Administration
Maintain the Audit and Assurance Calendars and ensure planned audits, assurance engagements, key milestones, deliverables, and deadlines are accurately captured and regularly updated.
Provide administrative and coordination support for internal, external, statutory, donor, and other audit and assurance engagements as assigned by the Compliance Manager.
Track audit timelines, milestones, information requests, deliverables, and deadlines.
Maintain organized audit files, reports, management letters, and other relevant audit documentation in the designated electronic filing system.
Support the preparation of audit status updates and reports.
Provide logistical and administrative support during audit and assurance engagements.
Compliance Monitoring and Reviews
Support the Compliance Manager and Compliance Officer in implementing compliance monitoring activities.
Participate in compliance reviews and monitoring activities as assigned.
Assist in collecting, organizing, and compiling information and documentation required for compliance reviews.
Conduct preliminary administrative checks of designated compliance folders to confirm that required documents have been uploaded and are appropriately named and organized.
Identify missing documents, filing gaps, or inconsistencies and escalate them to the Compliance team for review.
Support the documentation of observations, action points, and follow-up requirements under supervision.
Statutory and Regulatory Compliance Support
Maintain trackers and calendars for statutory, tax, and other regulatory compliance requirements across AWF operations.

Recently, The Commission approved twenty seven programmes ranging from undergraduate, masters to PhD levels. Located at the heart of the Lower Eastern Region, and situated only a Kilometre away from Machakos City along Machakos/Wote Road, the University is destined to continue its growth trajectory to World Class status in the near future.

Job Description
Primary Health Care (PHC) is the foundation of Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and the cornerstone of resilient, equitable, and people-centred health systems. Kenya has made significant progress in strengthening PHC through investments in community health, Primary Care Networks (PCNs), digital health infrastructure, health financing reforms, and an enabling policy environment, including the Digital Health Act (2023), the Primary Health Care Act (2023), and the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025–2030). Despite these advances, frontline health workers continue to face increasing workloads, growing disease complexity, fragmented information systems, and limited access to timely clinical and operational decision support. Routine digital systems have substantially improved data capture and reporting but have yet to consistently transform data into actionable intelligence that improves service delivery and patient outcomes.
Horizon1000 (H1000) is a multi-year initiative to deploy contextually grounded, ethically designed AI solutions, including AI-powered Clinical Decision Support Systems, across primary healthcare systems in Kenya, as part of a bigger program in Africa. The initiative seeks to support governments in deploying safe, effective, and scalable AI-enabled clinical and health system tools that improve the quality, efficiency, and equity of PHC while ensuring that technology strengthens rather than replaces frontline health workers.
As the lead implementation partner, Amref Health Africa is responsible for coordinating country-level implementation, stakeholder engagement, operational delivery, programme management, evidence generation, and long-term sustainability while ensuring alignment with national priorities, donor expectations, and responsible AI principles. Through this work, Horizon1000 aims to demonstrate a scalable model for integrating AI into public-sector primary healthcare that can strengthen health systems across Kenya and inform responsible AI implementation throughout Africa.
About the Role
The Senior Technical Advisor – Horizon1000 provides strategic and operational leadership for the implementation, coordination, and delivery of the Horizon1000 Kenya programme. Reporting to the Senior Programme Manager, the position is responsible for leading the day-to-day implementation of the programme across participating counties while ensuring that all technical, operational, financial, governance, and partnership activities are delivered on time, within scope, and in accordance with donor, government, and institutional requirements.
The Senior Technical Advisor ensures that programme implementation is evidence-driven, government-led, and responsive to evolving operational realities. The role oversees implementation planning, workplan execution, budget management, risk mitigation, quality assurance, stakeholder coordination, and performance monitoring while fostering strong relationships with the Ministry of Health, Digital Health Agency, county governments, development partners, and implementing organizations.
Operating at the intersection of primary healthcare, artificial intelligence, digital health, implementation science, and health systems strengthening, the STA balances innovation with operational excellence to ensure that AI-enabled solutions are safely integrated into routine service delivery. The role promotes responsible AI principles by embedding ethical governance, transparency, equity, interoperability, human oversight, and continuous learning throughout implementation while ensuring that technology enhances frontline decision-making and strengthens public-sector health systems rather than creating parallel structures.
This role requires exceptional programme leadership, strategic and systems thinking, strong project management capability, government engagement experience, partnership coordination, digital health expertise, and the ability to lead complex multi-stakeholder initiatives in rapidly evolving environments. The STA will play a central role in positioning Kenya as a global leader in the responsible implementation of Artificial Intelligence for Primary Health Care and in generating implementation models that inform future scale-up across Africa.
Key Responsibilities
Programme Delivery & Management
Lead the day-to-day planning, coordination, and implementation of the Horizon1000 Kenya programme, ensuring delivery against scope, approved workplans, milestones, budgets, and donor commitments.
Translate programme strategy into structured annual and quarterly implementation plans, ensuring alignment with Ministry of Health priorities, county health plans, and national digital health strategies.
Manage the project implementation team and collaborate with other Amref Programs in the delivery of H1000 project
Coordinate implementation across all workstreams, including AI use case identification, solution deployment, responsible AI governance, implementation science, monitoring and evaluation, capacity strengthening, and sustainability planning.
Monitor programme progress against agreed deliverables, proactively identifying implementation bottlenecks and coordinating timely corrective actions.
Provide regular implementation updates, strategic recommendations, and risk assessments to the Senior Programme Manager and programme governance structures.
Ensure programme resources are effectively coordinated to maximize implementation efficiency, learning, and long-term health systems impact.
AI Implementation & Operational Delivery
Lead the operational coordination of AI-enabled solutions across participating counties, ensuring that implementation remains clinically relevant, user-centred, and aligned with routine Primary Health Care workflows.
Coordinate human-centred design activities, workflow assessments, user research, and use case prioritization in collaboration with county governments, technology partners, and frontline health workers.
Oversee phased deployment of AI-enabled solutions, ensuring implementation follows structured rollout plans that prioritize learning, adoption, quality improvement, and sustainability.
Coordinate readiness assessments, onboarding activities, user training, mentorship, and post-deployment support to strengthen adoption and effective utilization of AI-enabled tools.
Work closely with consortium partners, technology developers, and implementation teams to ensure AI solutions integrate effectively within Kenya's digital health ecosystem through the Digital Health Superhighway.
Ensure implementation activities consistently strengthen existing government systems and avoid creating parallel digital health structures.
Support continuous refinement of implementation approaches based on user feedback, implementation evidence, operational analytics, and evolving programme priorities.
Government & Stakeholder Engagement
Serve as the primary operational focal point for Horizon1000 implementation with the Ministry of Health, Digital Health Agency, county governments, regulatory institutions, and other government stakeholders.
Coordinate engagement with County Implementation Teams (CITs), health facility leadership, frontline health workers, professional associations, and implementing partners.
Facilitate national and county technical working groups, programme review meetings, co-creation workshops, implementation planning sessions, and governance forums.
Strengthen government ownership by ensuring H1000 is embedded within existing national and county health systems, policies, governance structures, and planning processes.
Foster effective collaboration across consortium partners, research institutions, technology developers, donors, and implementing organizations to ensure coordinated programme delivery.
Support policy dialogue and stakeholder engagement that promote responsible AI adoption, interoperability, digital health governance, and long-term institutionalization of programme outputs.
Responsible AI Governance & Quality Assurance
Ensure responsible AI principles, ethical safeguards, and patient safety considerations are integrated throughout programme implementation.
Coordinate implementation of recommendations from the Responsible AI & Ethics Committee, Technical and Scientific Advisory Group (TSAG), and other governance structures.
Support compliance with Kenya's Digital Health Act, Data Protection Act, National AI Strategy, Ministry of Health guidance, and other applicable legal, ethical, and regulatory frameworks.
Ensure ethical concerns, implementation risks, and operational issues identified by frontline users or stakeholders are documented, escalated, and addressed appropriately.
Promote implementation approaches that prioritize transparency, human oversight, explainability, fairness, inclusiveness, and continuous learning across all AI-enabled interventions.
Maintain quality assurance standards for programme implementation, ensuring technical excellence, operational consistency, and adherence to donor and institutional requirements.
Qualifications
Experience
Five (5) or more years of progressively responsible experience managing multi-stakeholder programmes in digital health, health systems strengthening, Artificial Intelligence, or international development, including at least two (2) years of supervisory or project leadership experience, with a Master’s degree, OR

Autonomous Relationship Management — Schools and SMEs
The SRM independently manages a mixed loan book covering school and SME clients in equal measure. School loans carry a relatively stable risk profile due to the fixed, community rooted nature of school
premises and directors. SME loans require a different and sharper vigilance — owner managed businesses can change hands, relocate, or deteriorate quickly. The SRM is expected to manage both sub-portfolios with discipline and to apply the level of scrutiny each demands.
Own and manage a mixed school and SME loan portfolio, self organising the work plan to balance origination, monitoring, and collections activity across both client types. Conduct independent weekly portfolio health reviews — segmenting school and SME exposures separately — and submit structured reports to the Commercial Manager by COB every Friday. Proactively flag at-risk SME accounts at the first sign of stress (missed repayments, business closure, owner unavailability), before delinquency thresholds are breached.
Maintain portfolio at risk (PAR 30) within institutional thresholds across the total portfolio, with separate tracking for school and SME sub-portfolios.
School Client Acquisition and Relationship Management
The SRM is expected to operate as a trusted financial advisor to school directors, not merely a loan officer. This means cultivating long-term relationships, anticipating needs across loan cycles, and positioning Jackfruit solutions ahead of competitors.
Identify and onboard new schools, with a focus on complex or larger ticket opportunities. Conduct multi-cycle relationship management — maintaining contact with schools between loan cycles to support retention and repeat borrowing.
Represent Jackfruit at activations, school association events, county education forums, and community touchpoints to build the brand and generate referrals.
Develop tailored value propositions for different school segments (early childhood, primary, secondary, vocational).
Large SME Client Acquisition — Segment Focus and Quality Standards
Jackfruit's SME lending targets businesses with recurring cash flows, identifiable assets, and verifiable operating history. The SRM is responsible for ensuring both small and large SMEs and quality large SME clients are originated — not volume for its own sake. The following segments are in scope:
Retail traders with demonstrable stock turnover and a stable business location. Agribusiness and value addition enterprises with a defined production or trading cycle. Service providers with identifiable client contracts or a track record of repeat revenue. Transport operators with verifiable assets (vehicles, logbooks) and route consistency. Light manufacturers with documented production capacity and sales channels. Education linked SMEs (school suppliers, uniform traders, stationery vendors) who operate within the school ecosystem.
The SRM must apply a discerning eye to SME client selection. Unlike schools — which are fixed in the community — SME owners can relocate, pivot their business model, or become unreachable. The SRM is expected to screen for business sustainability, owner character, and community rootedness before any
loan is recommended, and to maintain ongoing physical contact with SME clients throughout the loan cycle.
SME Credit Assessment and Risk Ownership
SME appraisals require deeper investigative work than school appraisals. Audited financials are rarely available; the SRM must construct a credit picture from bank statements, sales records, supplier relationships, stock observations, and direct owner interviews. Character assessment is not a soft skill in SME lending — it is a credit variable.
Conduct full SME credit appraisals covering: business registration and licensing, PIN certificate and tax compliance, 12-month bank statement analysis, sales and purchase records review, cash flow projection stress testing, existing debt obligations, and inventory or stock verification.
Complete physical business location verification for every SME applicant — no exceptions. Document trading premises, stock levels, and asset conditions with photographs. Assess owner character and community standing through reference checks, supplier and customer interviews, and credit bureau review.
Screen all SME applicants against KYC/AML requirements, the Jackfruit exclusion list, and environmental and social risk compliance criteria.
Confirm minimum 3 years of verifiable operating history before recommending any SME loan. Prepare written credit summaries for borderline or higher-value SME cases for Investment Committee (IC) review.
Monitor fund utilisation post-disbursement for SME clients through structured business visits within 30 days of disbursement, with photographic evidence.
Collateral and Security Management
SME lending frequently involves physical collateral — movable assets, stock, or property. The SRM must be competent in assessing collateral quality and in coordinating the registration and management of security.
Coordinate valuation reports and proof of ownership documentation for all collateral backed SME loans.
Ensure insurance cover is in place for financed assets where required.
Liaise with the legal and collections team on chattel registration and charge documents. Identify and escalate any deterioration in collateral value or client asset base during the loan cycle.
Collections and Delinquency Management
The SRM leads first-line collections across their full portfolio. For SME loans, early intervention is critical — waiting for a second or third missed payment in the SME segment often means the window for recovery has already narrowed significantly.
Initiate first-line recovery contact within 24 hours of a missed payment for any SME client. Conduct physical visits to SME client premises for all accounts moving toward PAR 7, before PAR 30 is reached.
Escalate to the collections team with a written case summary when internal recovery efforts are not resolving within agreed timelines.
Peer Mentorship and SME Knowledge Transfer
The SRM plays a formal mentorship role within the field team. Given the complexity of SME credit work, a key part of this mentorship is building SME lending competence in Junior and Senior SSLs who are newer to the asset class.
Act as an assigned buddy or technical mentor for new SSL hires during their first 90 days, with particular focus on SME appraisal techniques, business verification, and character assessment. Lead or co-lead at least one regional knowledge sharing session per quarter — topics should include SME credit case studies, delinquency turnaround stories, or sector-specific insights (e.g. agribusiness seasonality, transport asset risk).
Provide informal field coaching to Junior and Senior SSLs upon request or at the direction of the Commercial Manager — without formal line management responsibility.
Market Intelligence and Product Feedback
Document and share competitive intelligence on a quarterly basis, covering both school and SME lending competitors.
Participate in product feedback sessions when invited by the CFO or Commercial Manager, representing the voice of the field on both product lines.
Identify and flag new SME segments, geographies, or loan product opportunities based on field observations.
Academic and Professional Qualifications
Relevant diploma from a recognised institution (minimum requirement).
Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field is an added advantage.
Certificate in basic computer skills.
Professional certification in credit or microfinance (e.g. ACCA, KASNEB, AMFI-K) is an added advantage.
Experience
Minimum 3 years of field sales and credit experience, with demonstrated exposure to both school financing and SME lending.
Demonstrable track record of consistent target attainment at Senior SSL Level 1 or Level 2 (or equivalent), with portfolio quality metrics within institutional thresholds.

Job Description:
About the Role
Our client, a leading organisation in the manufacturing sector, is seeking to recruit a Plant Administrator to support the efficient administrative, financial, logistics, and operational activities at one of its manufacturing facilities.
Reporting to the Plant Manager, the successful candidate will coordinate product dispatch activities, manage driver allowances and fuel administration, maintain accurate financial records and reconciliations, support regulatory compliance, and ensure effective day-to-day site administration.
Key Responsibilities
Dispatch Coordination & Documentation
Coordinate product dispatch activities and ensure the availability of required dispatch documentation.
Process trip allowance and fuel requests for drivers.
Coordinate truck and driver allocations.
Ensure accurate and timely completion of delivery notes, weighbridge tickets, consignment documents, and other dispatch paperwork.
Maintain accurate records of product movements in the ERP system to support sales invoicing and inventory control.
Driver Allowances & Fuel Management
Process daily driver trip allowances based on approved routes and distances.
Manage fuel allocation requests and reconcile fuel consumption against completed trips.
Monitor fuel efficiency and investigate anomalies or excessive consumption.
Ensure timely and accurate processing of driver allowance payments.
Maintain comprehensive records of allowances and fuel disbursements.
Work with Finance and Logistics teams to resolve discrepancies and support cost-control measures.
Dispatch & Mileage Reporting
Prepare regular dispatch and mileage reports.
Reconcile dispatch reports from relevant systems and ensure variances are identified and resolved.
Maintain records relating to truck fuelling, mileage, and trip details.
Coordinate documentation requests to support logistics and finance reporting.
Ensure dispatch records are accurate, current, and audit-ready.
Financial Reporting, Reconciliation & Petty Cash
Prepare monthly reconciliations of plant balance sheet schedules.
Manage petty cash disbursements, reconciliations, and replenishment requests.
Maintain accurate cash counts and ensure the imprest system is properly managed.
Coordinate with the Chief Accountant and Plant Manager on financial reporting, approvals, and reconciliations.
Prepare payment requests and coordinate with Head Office for financial approvals.
Ensure financial documentation is complete, accurate, and audit-ready.
Regulatory & Statutory Compliance
Ensure timely fulfilment of plant statutory and regulatory requirements.
Maintain compliance documentation, permits, medical reports, and other relevant records.
Liaise with the Compliance function on statutory requirements.
Coordinate with external regulators regarding required documentation and permits.
Monitor compliance deadlines and ensure requirements are addressed within stipulated timelines.
Administration & General Worker Supervision
Manage the plant leave calendar and ensure adherence to approved leave schedules.
Coordinate correspondence between the plant and Head Office and ensure timely responses.
Supervise general and casual workers, including outsourced staff involved in housekeeping and site maintenance.
Ensure administrative actions are completed within agreed timelines.
Maintain overall site administrative compliance and operational efficiency.
Qualifications & Experience
Degree or Diploma in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Logistics, or a related field.
CPA certification is required.
Minimum 3 years’ accounting experience, preferably within a manufacturing environment.
Experience in dispatch coordination, driver allowances, fuel administration, and logistics administration.
Experience working with SAP or other ERP systems is an advantage.
Experience with dispatch/accounting systems such as Soradius will be an added advantage.
Strong understanding of financial reconciliations, petty cash, documentation, and reporting.
Key Competencies
Strong numerical and analytical skills.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong organisational and record-keeping skills.
Ability to coordinate multiple operational and administrative activities.
Good stakeholder management and communication skills.
Strong integrity and accountability.
Ability to identify and resolve discrepancies.
Good understanding of audit-ready documentation and compliance requirements.
Ability to supervise and coordinate support staff.

Ensure all warehouse transactions are accurately and timely processed in SPEED.
Monitor system transactions and identify errors, discrepancies, duplicate entries, and data inconsistencies.
Support users in resolving SPEED-related operational and transactional issues.
Train and coach new and existing SPEED users on system procedures and best practices.
Monitor user compliance with approved SPEED processes and controls.
Conduct regular reconciliation of SPEED records against physical stock and warehouse documentation.

Generate and review SPEED reports to support warehouse operations, inventory control, and management decision-making.
Ensure proper audit trails and documentation for all system transactions and adjustments.
Support stock-taking exercises, audits, investigations, and reconciliation processes.
Identify opportunities to improve warehouse processes through effective use of SPEED.
Escalate critical system or operational issues that may affect warehouse productivity, stock integrity, or customer service.
Maintain confidentiality and integrity of system and customer information.
Perform any other duties related to SPEED administration and warehouse operations as assigned.
Key Competencies
SPEED system proficiency
Warehouse and inventory management
Data accuracy and attention to detail
Troubleshooting and problem-solving
User training and support
Reconciliation and analytical skills
Process improvement
Communication and coordination
Accountability and integrity
Ability to work under pressure
Qualifications And Experience
Diploma or degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Information Technology, Warehouse Management, or a related field.
At least 2–3 years' experience in warehouse, logistics, commodity handling, or a similar environment.
Demonstrated experience using SPEED or a comparable warehouse management system.
Strong understanding of warehouse processes, inventory control, stock reconciliation, and documentation.
Good Microsoft Excel and data-analysis skills.
Experience training or supporting other system users.

Job Title: Project Officer - NYOTA Refugee Business Development Services Mentor
Job Description:
Overall purpose of the role:
DRC has submitted an Expression of Interest (EOI) for The National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) Project, supported by the World Bank and implemented by the Government of Kenya through the Micro and Small Enterprises Authority (MSEA), that aims to expand employment and entrepreneurship opportunities for vulnerable youth. In anticipation of being shortlisted and invited to submit a full proposal, DRC is launching this recruitment process to identify suitably qualified candidates for the proposed key positions. Any subsequent engagement will be conditional on DRC progressing to the proposal stage and ultimately being awarded the assignment.
Within this anticipated assignment, the BDS Mentor will guide and support refugee youth entrepreneurs through structured mentorship, drawing on practical business experience to strengthen their decision-making, resilience and capacity to develop viable and sustainable enterprises. The role will provide ongoing advice and encouragement, support participants to address business challenges, and help strengthen market linkages and progress towards their entrepreneurial goals.
Duties & Responsibilities:
Structured mentorship
Provide regular one-to-one and/or small-group mentorship to refugee youth entrepreneurs, including scheduled check-ins and progress reviews.
Reinforce BDS training content, help participants troubleshoot business challenges, refine plans and remain accountable to agreed business goals.
Share practical lessons from real business experience and help participants avoid common mistakes in their entrepreneurial journey
Business guidance and market linkages
Advise mentees on relevant areas including strategic planning, financial management, marketing, operations and day-to-day business decision-making.
Support linkages to local entrepreneurs, business groups, markets, finance and other BDS or complementary services where appropriate.
Contribute to community business forums, peer-learning spaces and other networking opportunities intended to expand market access and social cohesion.
Motivation, inclusion and safe support
Act as an excellent listener and provide a respectful space for mentees to discuss challenges, ideas and progress.
Provide encouragement and emotional support that helps mentees remain motivated and resilient while respecting professional boundaries and referral procedures.
Support inclusive mentorship approaches for women and persons with disabilities and demonstrate cultural competence in refugee and displacement-affected settings.
Documentation and coordination
Document mentorship contacts, content and progress in the formats required by the project and support verification of sessions delivered.
Coordinate with the Team Leader, BDS Delivery Specialists and DRC project staff to identify follow-up needs and relevant referrals.
Participate in mentor training, supervision and reporting arrangements established for the assignment
Experience and Technical Competence
Extensive practical experience in the business world, including successful experience running a business.
Strong knowledge of core business areas such as strategic planning, financial management, marketing and operations.
Strong listening, coaching and interpersonal skills, with the ability to provide practical guidance and constructive support.
Ability to conduct regular progress reviews and help entrepreneurs adjust plans and stay on track with their goals.
Knowledge of the realities of doing business in refugee/camp or displacement-affected settings is highly relevant to the assignment.
The mentor cohort must include demonstrated competence in supporting entrepreneurs with disabilities and meaningful representation of female mentors; DRC therefore particularly welcomes applications from women and candidates with relevant disability-inclusion experience.
Education
Minimum secondary school education or equivalent.
Certificate, diploma or other vocational/professional training in business, entrepreneurship, finance, marketing, management or a related field is an advantage.
Practical business and mentoring experience is central to the role
Language
Ability to mentor participants in relevant languages used in refugee settings.
Proficiency in Somali is highly desirable, particularly for work with refugee communities in Dadaab

Job Description:
SCOPE OF WORK
:
The Registered Nurse - Midwife is responsible for the day-to-day implementation of Maternal and Neonatal Care, in the maternity unit within IRC supported Health facilities. S/he will work closely with other maternity staff including Doctors, Nurses, Clinical Officer, Auxiliary nurses and by proxy with the theatre staff, to ensure quality of care for patients and babies admitted in the unit and aim to promote quality of care for Gynae and or Emergency obstetric and Neonatal Care patients in the IRC supported health facilities.
Responsibilities/Main Duties:
Quality maternal and perinatal care: Able to offer high quality nursing care during admissions in maternity, hospital stay and discharging mothers and newborns. On spot/ Daily assessment of general /clinical condition, early identification of complications, Sound clinical judgement call for help, communicating promptly, as you stabilize the mother/newborn. Able to assess ready for discharge of mothers and their newborns, prepare their documentation.
Antenatal Care: Conducting regular check-ups, monitoring maternal and foetal vital signs, ordering and interpreting diagnostic tests, and providing health education on nutrition and birth preparedness.
Labor and Delivery Management: Monitoring the progress of labour using a labour care guide, providing physical and emotional support, administering medications as prescribed (e.g. antibiotics, uterotonics, analgesics), conducting normal vaginal deliveries, AMSTEL, being part of the MDT conducting difficult deliveries breech, AVDs which are rare and performing neonatal resuscitation.
Postnatal Care: Monitoring mothers for signs of complications (e.g., haemorrhage, infection), assessing uterine involution and lochia, assisting with early ambulation, and educating mothers on breastfeeding, perineal care, and post-partum family planning.
Emergency Response: Early Identification of obstetric and neonatal complications and instituting timely and appropriate interventions and escalating care to medical officers.
Referral: Able to process patient referral documents, prepare equipment’s and medication for use on transit. Accompany patient during referral within hospital departments or during external movement to a healthcare
Documentation and Reporting: Maintaining accurate and complete documentation of your work, up-to-date clinical records, patient charts, and reports in EMR to include Ministry of Health reports, in compliance with healthcare regulations in utilizing and sharing data for decision making.
Continuous quality Improvement and Safety: Executing nursing care model and utilizing results with multi-disciplinary team to improve patient management. Adhering to infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, participating in MPDSR audits and quality improvement activities, Respectful maternity care and ensuring a safe clinical environment for staff, patients and relatives.
Skills: Key skills include excellent clinical acumen (Certificate in EMONC training), critical thinking, communication, problem-solving, negotiating and a compassionate, patient-centered approach to care and being a team player.
Able to communicate fluently verbally and written. Use of SBAR during hand over /referral.
Leadership and management: Able to cover calls, hospital covering, performing doctor’s round, ward management, team leader able to make sound judgements in patient care and staff management. Attending Meetings, CMEs and trainings as required.
Accountability: Able to clear after every procedure, Equipment and instrument processing as per national guidelines. Equipment inventory and safety to include functional emergency crash cart in every shift.
Ensure emergency preparedness trays and equipment inventory is in place in maternity and items monitored and are updated daily through a structured handover during every shift.
Executing any other duty allocated by your supervisor.
Reporting/Communication:
Responsible for compiling daily Nursing care activity reports while handing over in shifts.
Responsible for accurate record keeping, ordering and accountability of equipment and supplies.
Attend ward meeting, monthly hospital meetings and or facilitate Continuous Medical Education
Ensure that all admissions, discharges, transfers and deaths are properly documented and recorded as they occur and participate in respective mortality audits.
Report any significant changes in clinical operations to the supervisor.
Any other duties assigned by supervisor.
Operations:
Maintain departmental equipment, suction machines, resuscitators, various procedure sets are maintained and always in good condition and submit regular inventory reports of the same.
Report on any significant changes in operations to the head nurse.
Systems Compliance and Improvement:
Ensure IRC-Kenya program specific finance, logistics, IT, security, communications and human resource/administration policies and procedures are adhered to.
Comply with any new procedures and guidelines designated in circulation from SMT and or Field team Management.
Confidentiality:
Ensuring the nondisclosure of any information whatsoever relating to the practices and business of IRC acquired in the course of duty, to any other person or organization without authority, except in the normal execution of duty.
Note:
The role of the Midwife cannot be limited to the specific duties and tasks detailed herein. The success of the IRC’s humanitarian mission is the highest priority and all issues which arise must be addressed accordingly. Therefore, the Midwife will be required to manage all unforeseen issues and circumstances and remain flexible to perform other duties, as and when required.
Qualifications, Skills and Experience:
Kenya Registered Community Health Nurse (KRCHN)/Kenya Registered Midwife. (KRM) from a recognized Nursing Training Institution
Registered with the Nursing Council of Kenya with valid practicing licence.
More than 2 years of clinical maternity ward experience in a busy facility.
Added advantage
Previous work experience in a limited resource setting is an added advantage.
Ability to speak local language will be an added advantage
